title: Global Verdier duality at the point
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions of [def-pod-conventions] (so $X_0$
is smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure
dimension $d$, not necessarily proper). The statement below also
holds verbatim for a smooth, proper, geometrically connected $k$-scheme
$X$ of pure dimension $d$ not assumed to descend to $k_0$ (see
[thm-sf-global-duality]). Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. For the admissible structure
morphism $a_X:X\to s$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK),
$$

with the cohomology functors
of the fixed coefficient stage. It is natural in $K$ and compatible
with shifts. For a site-perfect
$K$, it is also compatible with finite coefficient reduction and
scalar extension under the smooth orientation and its coefficient
comparisons. At $K=\Lambda_X$ it identifies
$R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X)^\vee$ with $R\Gamma(X,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$.

proof.text: Instantiate the Verdier exchange [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] at $f=a_X:X\to s$, $Y=s$, and $M=K$. The smooth separated finite-type scheme and the admissibility of $a_X$ are given by [def-pod-conventions]. The remaining structure morphism is $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$. It satisfies [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]: take the identity compactification, cohomological-dimension bound $0$, identity right adjoint with identity unit and counit, and interval shifts $c^- = c^+ =0$; all coefficient comparisons are identities. Thus all three admissibility hypotheses of the exchange hold. It gives the canonical isomorphism $e_{\Lambda,K}:D_s(Ra_{X!}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X*}D_XK$, natural in $K$ and compatible with the specified coefficient comparisons and shifts.

Put $C=Ra_{X!}K$ and $T=Ra_{X*}D_XK$. Their finite-Tor point domains follow from [thm-sf-ctf-stability], also integrally and at the field stages. Apply [lem-pod-point-exchange-coefficient-realization] to $e$ from step 1: $g=\operatorname{Fib}_s(e)j_{\Lambda,C}^{-1}$ is a natural isomorphism with the specified shifts. By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], its source and target are precisely $R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee$ and $R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$.

For site-perfect $K$, [lem-pod-smooth-oriented-exchange-comparisons] supplies the site square with $u_Q:Q_sC\cong Ra_{X!}Q_XK$ and its actual operation comparisons. Apply [lem-pod-point-exchange-coefficient-realization] to this square. Its equation $Vq(g)=g'(w^{-1})^\vee b_{Q,c}$ is the required coefficient-duality square. The orientation equations and the last assertion of the site-comparison lemma identify it with the stipulated square under $\eta_X$.

For the unit object, [def-pod-conventions] gives $\mathbb D_X\Lambda_X=R\mathcal Hom_X(\Lambda_X,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$. The unit Hom identity is evaluation at $1$: $h\mapsto h(1)$, with inverse $x\mapsto(r\mapsto rx)$. Since internal Hom from the free rank-one unit is already the identity exact functor, its derived functor is the identity as well. Thus $\mathbb D_X\Lambda_X\cong\omega_{X,\Lambda}$, and substitution in step 2 gives $R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X)^\vee\cong R\Gamma(X,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$.

No step above identifies $Ra_{X!}$ with $Ra_{X*}$, so descended $X$ needs no properness. For smooth proper geometrically connected $X/k$ without descent, [thm-sf-global-duality] supplies the canonical isomorphism, naturality, shifts, coefficient comparisons and unit specialization using the constructible exceptional adjoint. Its coefficient-complex interpretation is the fibre of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The unconditional orientation assertion of [lem-pod-smooth-oriented-exchange-comparisons] identifies those comparisons under the smooth orientation, restricting coefficient compatibility to site-perfect $K$. Properness is not used to infer ambient admissibility.

Use the Poincare duality conventions of [def-pod-conventions] (so $X_0$
is smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure
dimension $d$, not necessarily proper). The statement below also
holds verbatim for a smooth, proper, geometrically connected $k$-scheme
$X$ of pure dimension $d$ not assumed to descend to $k_0$ (see
[thm-sf-global-duality]). Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. For the admissible structure
morphism $a_X:X\to s$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK),
$$

with the cohomology functors
of the fixed coefficient ring. It is natural in $K$ and compatible
with shifts. For a site-perfect
$K$, it is also compatible with finite coefficient reduction and
scalar extension under the smooth orientation and its coefficient
comparisons. At $K=\Lambda_X$ it identifies
$R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda_X)^\vee$ with $R\Gamma(X,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$.

proof.text:
Apply the independently proved exchange [fix-cor-verdier-exchange]
to $f=a_X$ and the coefficient object at $s$:

$$
D_sRa_{X!}K\cong Ra_{X*}D_XK.
$$

By [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], $D_s$ is the derived
coefficient dual. Apply the point equivalence of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]; the two resulting global
functors are those of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].
This proves the asserted isomorphism and its naturality and shift
compatibility. Its construction uses only tensor–Hom adjunction,
the compact-support projection formula, and the adjunction for
$Ra_{X!}$; it does not use global Poincare duality.
For $K$ site-perfect in the sense of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex], the tensor, internal-Hom,
evaluation, and cohomology comparisons are
[lem-fix-operation-reduction]. The smooth dualizing object and
its counit reduce compatibly by
[thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]. Each constituent of the
adjunction comparison therefore commutes with coefficient change,
so their composite does too. Finally $D_X\Lambda_X=\omega_X$
by tensor–Hom evaluation of the unit object, giving the specialization.
Properness of $X_0$ is used nowhere above: the exchange
[fix-cor-verdier-exchange] needs only that $a_X$ is exceptionally
admissible, $Ra_{X!}$ and $Ra_{X*}$ enter as different functors with no
comparison between them, and the smooth dualizing object and its finite
reduction ([thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]) are stated for smooth
separated morphisms. The same argument applies word for word to a smooth
proper $X$ over $k$ that is not defined over $k_0$, which is the proper
case of [thm-sf-global-duality].
